scenarios.description: APPLY -> PENDINGFORASSIGNMENT. Citizen with phone AND email; default locale. Three seeded CITIZEN rows (SMS/WHATSAPP/EMAIL); WHATSAPP has an approved Twilio provider template so templateId + positional contentVariables ride along.
Same transition, citizen has NO email: the EMAIL row is contact-gated away (no phantom send), SMS + WHATSAPP still emit.
Citizen carries no uuid: the subscriber key falls back to service.accountId. The mobile already starts with '+', so the countryCode is NOT prefixed again.

ASSIGN -> PENDINGATLME with a named assignee (workflow.assignes[0]) resolved through egov-user, plus HRMS + MDMS ComplaintHierarchy so {emp_name}/{emp_department}/{emp_designation} resolve. Six envelopes: CITIZEN x3 and EMPLOYEE x3. The EMPLOYEE WHATSAPP row has NO provider template in the seed (they are all CITIZEN) so it emits with no templateId for an auditable bridge-side SKIP.
REASSIGN -> PENDINGFORREASSIGNMENT. The seeded rows author fromState=PENDINGATLME, which the Kafka path never supplies, so they match anyway (documentation-only).
RESOLVE -> RESOLVED, citizen only.
REJECT -> REJECTED; workflow.comments becomes {additional_comments}.
REOPEN -> PENDINGFORASSIGNMENT, citizen only.

RATE -> CLOSEDAFTERRESOLUTION. workflow.assignes is empty, so the assignee comes from the LAST ASSIGN in workflow history (egov-workflow-v2 ?history=true) and is then hydrated from egov-user. EMPLOYEE-only routing; {rating} is filled.
RATE -> CLOSEDAFTERREJECTION has NO routing row in the seed: zero envelopes. This is the transition the design calls out as invisible today (no ledger row at all).

The citizen's user-preference is hi_IN: body, subject and Twilio provider template all come from the hi_IN rows and contact.locale is hi_IN. NOTE the placeholder VALUES are still English - they are localized once per event from RequestInfo.msgId, not per recipient. No assignee, so the EMPLOYEE rows resolve to nobody and the CITIZEN body keeps its literal {emp_name}/{emp_designation}/{emp_department} braces.
Preference fr_FR has no template: body/subject/templateKey fall back to the default locale (en_IN) and so does the WhatsApp provider template - but contact.locale still carries the recipient's fr_FR.

RequestInfo.msgId carries hi_IN while the recipient has no preference: the TEMPLATE is en_IN but {complaint_type}/{status} are localized in hi_IN. Pins the split between placeholder localization (msgId, per event) and template locale (per recipient).

Seeded ASSIGN rows PLUS an extra PGR_LME SMS row. The pool has three holders paged two at a time: emp-jane (also the assignee - deduped on (channel, subscriberKey), audience deliberately not in the key), a holder with neither phone nor email (dropped at pool resolution) and lme-brian (emitted). Seven envelopes.

A single PGR_LME SMS row with assigneeOnly=true and a named assignee: the pool is not searched at all and the row collapses to the assignee. NOTE contact.type is EMPLOYEE (from assignee resolution) while the TEMPLATE is still looked up under PGR_LME.
Same row, but nothing names an assignee (no workflow.assignes, no history): rather than notifying no one, the row falls through to the full role pool.

Four rows the router must drop and two it must keep: active=false, an unknown channel (PUSH), the non-notifiable AUTO_ESCALATE pseudo-audience, a blank audience, and a row for another businessService. Only the WHATSAPP and EMAIL CITIZEN rows emit.

The only Twilio row for this key is approvalStatus=pending: PGR still EMITS the WHATSAPP envelope with no templateId/contentVariables so the bridge can write an auditable SKIPPED / NB_TEMPLATE_NOT_APPROVED row instead of dropping it silently.

EMAIL bodies HTML-escape substituted values (they are delivered as raw HTML); the subject is plain text and is NOT escaped. The localized complaint type carries &, " and < so both sides of the rule are visible in one envelope.
An EMAIL template with a null subject: Novu rejects a blank subject, so the service substitutes 'Complaint <serviceRequestId>'.

A routed (audience, channel) with a resolvable recipient but NO template in the recipient's locale nor the default: the recipient is skipped and nothing is emitted - today this is invisible downstream (no ledger row).
A pool holder with no uuid keys the subscriber on the phone number instead: subscriberId and transactionId carry the raw MSISDN (PII on the wire, masked only in the logs).

One template using all 13 placeholders with every source healthy (localization, the URL shortener, egov-user, HRMS and MDMS ComplaintHierarchy). Pins exactly what each token resolves to for a role-pool recipient.

Same template with egov-url-shortening throwing: {download_link} is BLANKED (never left as a literal brace) and every other placeholder survives - the defensive try/catch structure the design says must be preserved.

Same template with egov-localization throwing: {complaint_type} falls back to the raw service code, {status} to the raw applicationStatus, {ulb}/{ao_designation}/{emp_department}/{emp_designation} are left as literal braces, and id/date/rating/citizen_name/download_link/emp_name still resolve. This is the Twilio-21656 regression the base-placeholders-first ordering exists to prevent.

PGR's supervisor escalation (PGRConstants.ESCALATE, PENDINGATLME --ESCALATE--> PENDINGATLME) reaches this code through the same Kafka path as every other transition, but the shipped seed has NO routing row for it: the new supervisor is never told. Recorded as current behaviour, not endorsed - the escalation notification gap is real.
